26 Which list of regions of the electromagnetic spectrum is in order of increasing wavelength from
left to right?
A
gamma-ray  ultraviolet  infrared
B
infrared  microwave  ultraviolet
C
microwave  X-ray  infrared
D
X-ray  ultraviolet  gamma-ray

hints: Notice the question asks for increasing wavelength from left to right, so the shortest wavelength region must be on the left.
Recall the order of the main regions by wavelength: gamma-ray, then X-ray, then ultraviolet, then visible light, then infrared, then microwave, then radio wave.
Check each list to see if the second region is longer than the first and the third is longer than the second, especially where gamma-ray, ultraviolet and infrared appear.
walkthrough: Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing wavelength $\lambda$: gamma-ray, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio wave.
The question requires each step left to right to move to a longer wavelength and lower frequency, since $c = f\lambda$.
The gamma-ray to ultraviolet to infrared chain moves from about $10^{-12} \text{ m}$ to about $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to about $10^{-6} - 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, which is a continuous increase.
The other chains fail because ultraviolet is placed after microwave, microwave is placed before X-ray, or gamma-ray is placed after ultraviolet, all of which reverse the true order.
The only list that increases in wavelength at every step is gamma-ray to ultraviolet to infrared. This is option A

A.explanation: Gamma-ray has the shortest wavelength, ultraviolet is intermediate, and infrared is longer, so wavelength increases left to right.

B.explanation: Infrared to microwave is an increase, but ultraviolet has a much shorter wavelength than infrared so it cannot come after microwave.

C.explanation: Microwave has a long wavelength of order millimetres to centimetres, so it cannot come before X-ray and infrared.

D.explanation: X-ray to ultraviolet is an increase, but gamma-ray has the shortest wavelength of all so it cannot come last.
